scenario.title: Writing to a Club Organizer
scenario.description: You joined a local hiking club two months ago, and Mr. Tanaka organizes its weekend trips. The club has just announced that all future hikes will start at 6 a.m. on Saturdays, but you work a Saturday morning shift at a bakery.
scenario.subject: Question about the new hiking schedule
scenario.purpose: Explain a scheduling conflict and propose an alternative
keyPoints: Tell the organizer what you have enjoyed about the club
Explain why the new schedule is difficult for you
Suggest a change or an option that could help members in your situation

modelAnswer:
Dear Mr. Tanaka,

Thank you for organizing such wonderful trips over the past two months. The hike to Eagle Lake was the highlight of my summer, and I have made several new friends through the club.

I just read the announcement about the new 6 a.m. start time, and I am afraid it will be hard for me to keep participating. I work at a bakery every Saturday from five until noon, so I would miss nearly every outing. I understand that early starts help the group avoid the afternoon heat, though.

Would it be possible to hold one hike a month on Sunday instead? I suspect a few other members also have weekend jobs, so a Sunday option might keep more people involved. I would be glad to help plan the route for the first one.

Warm regards,
Priya

rubric.description: Expresses appreciation, explains the conflict with a concrete reason, and offers a realistic suggestion.
Clear progression with a friendly opening, a balanced explanation, and a constructive proposal.
Friendly yet respectful register for a club member; idiomatic phrasing and varied sentence types.
